posts.author: Rototiller
posts.text: The Latin preposition cum, means "with" or "together."  Over centuries, it entered the English language in two major ways: as a highly productive prefix (com- / con-) used to build vocabulary, and as a standalone loanword to combine roles or titles. exempli gratia: communicate, activist-cum-fashion designer Rachel Antonoff Ha en fin dag.
